title: PrivateNet usage-first licensing experiment with tiered emergency-patch SLA and consolidated SQ forwarding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Run a 6-week pricing and packaging experiment for PrivateNet (Private/VPC + on-prem) to validate a usage-first commercial construct. Hypothesis: offering a low base license fee + metered GPU-hour credits and a small pool of 'patch credits' for accelerated emergency upgrades will increase deal velocity for regulated customers while preserving predictable revenue. The experiment also pilots a consolidated Security Questionnaire (SQ) forwarding flow: auto-generate the first-pass SQ bundle and route to a dedicated sales-SQ queue for faster Q&A. We will test three entitlement lanes, measure conversion and support load, and iterate on upgrade cadence options (monthly scheduled vs quarterly with emergency patch lanes).
success_criteria: 5% lift in MQL->PO conversion for PrivateNet proposals during pilot window
Average TTV (time-to-vote) reduced by 20% for deals requiring SQ responses
Patch SLA adoption: >=40% of pilot customers choose the 'accelerated patch' lane at purchase
Support ticket volume per customer for upgrade-related issues does not increase by more than 10%
acceptance_criteria: Billing prototype able to invoice base license + GPU-credit consumption in sandbox
SQ auto-bundle template validated by security (sec-review signoff) and available to sales
Legal approves contract language for 'patch credits' and scheduled upgrade windows
Sales completes 10 pilot proposals using new entitlement lanes and provides feedback
rollout_plan: Week 0: finalize entitlement definitions and price bands; sign off with Finance and Legal
Week 1: implement billing prototype for metered credits in test environment; create SQ templates
Week 2: onboard 6 pilot customers (mix of mid-market and enterprise) via Solutions Engineering
Week 3-5: monitor usage, gather sales & security questionnaire telemetry, collect qualitative feedback
Week 6: analyze metrics, produce recommendations for standard product packaging and contract language
metrics: conversion_rate: MQL->PO for PrivateNet deals (pilot cohort vs baseline)
deal_velocity_days: average days from proposal to signed PO
sq_turnaround_hours: median time to complete initial SQ response
patch_lane_uptake_pct: percent of customers who purchased accelerated patch credits
support_load_delta: percent change in upgrade-related tickets per customer
decisions_made: Use three entitlement lanes: Base (monthly scheduled upgrades), Flex (quarterly upgrades + limited patch credits), Accelerated (monthly + larger patch pool)
Price anchors: base license set at 20% below current average enterprise on-prem anchor to test elasticity
SQ forwarding: create a single canonical answer set per common Qs and route complex items to security team
Telemetry: product runtime will emit upgrade-related events to Console to track patch SLA usage
open_questions: What is the optimal size of the initial patch credit pool to balance revenue and operational risk?
How should on-prem customers with air-gapped environments receive emergency patches? (offline patch appliance vs manual deliverable)
Can billing support prorated consumption across calendar months for GPU credits?
Do sales teams need an approval guardrail for deeply discounted commit bands?
stakeholders: Engineering Partner: Lina Gomez (Billing), Omar Farouk (Runtime)
risks: Revenue cannibalization if usage-first pricing is cheaper than current anchors for large customers
Operational load if many customers request emergency patches outside SLA windows
Security review delays could elongate sales cycles despite faster SQ automation
Billing edge-cases (proration, refunds for unused credits) may require manual intervention initially
notes: Kickoff 2026-02-12: Finance requested an FY26 revenue mapping for each price band. Security requested an initial sample SQ bundle for top-10 customers. Sales flagged two prospects (regulated fintech and healthcare ISV) to join pilot. Solutions Eng estimated 2 engineer-weeks to wire telemetry and 1 week for billing sandbox config. Legal proposed clause templates for patch credits; draft under review.
